claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you enquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are some specific rules that apply. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great - A-levels count as approved education. A few more questions to help me assess your eligibility:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to understand if you're responsible for Alex:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount (or more) towards his upkeep - such as for food, clothes, or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, started an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his A-levels at the moment - no job or benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 17 years old and is in approved education (A-levels), which means you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him until he turns 20, as long as he remains in approved education or training
- You live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, so you are responsible for him
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is not working 24+ hours per week, hasn't started an apprenticeship, and isn't receiving benefits in his own right

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it, you can continue to claim as long as Alex remains in approved education or training and is under 20.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
